name: Metlatónoc Mixtec
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Josserand 1983, Mixtec Dialect History (PhD, Tulane) — comparative phonology survey including Metlatonoc data; no variety-specific stress statement reachable (Wikipedia article checked: no stress section)

new_statements.quote: Tone is, for example, important in this dialect lexically as the distinguishing feature between otherwise homophonous forms. It is important morphologically as the contrastive feature between different aspects of the verb. It is important phonologically because it furnishes criteria for the placement of stress. [...] Within an effective verbal context (a stress group or series of them joined into a high-layered unit) voiced consonants carry the tone from one modulation to the next.
new_statements.citation: Overholt, Edward. 1961. The tonemic system of Guerrero Mixteco. In Benjamin F. Elson & Juan Comas (eds.), A William Cameron Townsend en el vigésimoquinto aniversario del Instituto Lingüístico de Verano, 597-626. México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano.
new_statements.locator: pp. 597-598 (introduction) and p. 601 (section 'Tone on Voiced Consonants'); scanned pages
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.rule_in_words: The language is a three-tone language; stress exists and its placement is said to be determined by tonal criteria, and a 'stress group' is a prosodic domain above the morpheme, but the source never states which syllable of the (disyllabic couplet) word carries stress. No placement rule is recoverable from any opened source for metl1238.
new_statements.domain_note: Overholt's unit is the 'morpheme pattern tone unit' (MPTU), basically the disyllabic couplet (CVCV, CVV, CVʔCV, CVʔV; derived CV and CVVV); 'stress group' is mentioned as a phrase-level unit. Data from Metlatónoc and San Rafael, Guerrero (idiolect of Esther López and three other speakers).
new_statements.identity_note: Overholt 1961 (data from Metlatónoc and San Rafael, Metlatónoc municipality) and Martínez Sánchez 2009 (Rancho Nuevo de la Democracia and Metlatónoc) both describe metl1238 proper. The only explicit stress-placement statement found in the group is Zylstra 1980 for Alacatlatzala Mixtec [mim], Glottolog alac1244 (Malinaltepec municipality), a separate language-level languoid under Guerrero Mixtec (guer1245); it is not a statement about metl1238. Glottolog's alternate-name list for metl1238 (Alacatlatzala, Alcozauca, Xochapa, Yoloxóchitl, Guerrero Mixtec) is inherited from ELCat's lumped 'Guerrero Mixtec' entry (10530) and does not make those varieties part of metl1238.

sources.note: Tone paper (three tonemes, nine couplet patterns, perturbation classes). Says only that tone 'furnishes criteria for the placement of stress' (p. 597-598) and mentions 'a stress group' as a prosodic domain (p. 601); never states which syllable is stressed. Full scanned grep for stress/accent/tress: only these two hits.

sources.citation: Zylstra, Carol F. 1980. Phonology and morphophonemics of the Mixtec of Alacatlatzala, Guerrero. SIL-Mexico Workpapers 4: 15-42. SISTER LANGUAGE: Alacatlatzala Mixtec [mim], Glottolog alac1244 (Malinaltepec municipality), not metl1238.
sources.note: p. 16: 'The phonological word... has only one stress. Stress falls on the initial syllable of the couplet except for the stress shift to the second syllable of the couplet when followed by the first person postclitic -i (5.2). Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of a three-syllable stem.' Rule 9 (Stress Shift) p. 32. Context only — different Glottolog language.

sources.citation: Martínez Sánchez, Joaquín José. 2009. Introducción a la poética de una lengua oral: el mixteco en la montaña baja (Guerrero, México). ELUA: Estudios de Lingüística, Universidad de Alicante 23: 161-201. doi:10.14198/ELUA2009.23.08. (Area: Rancho Nuevo de la Democracia and Metlatónoc.)
sources.note: Overview of all linguistic levels from a poetics angle; discusses the three tones and tone sandhi, nothing on stress/acento (grep for acent-, tónic-, prominen-: no relevant hit). Reference list announces a fuller book (Martínez Sánchez 2009, en prensa, 'La lengua mixteca en la Montaña Baja').
Consonant/vowel tables only; no tone or stress information.
